claims.claim: Adult diabetes fell to 15.6% in 2023, down from 18.3% in 2019.
claims.source: IKU MOH NHMS 2023 Fact Sheet https://iku.nih.gov.my/images/nhms2023/fact-sheet-nhms-2023.pdf ; NHMS 2019 Fact Sheet ; Mat Rifin et al., Scientific Reports 2025 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-08311-9
claims.correction: Avoid implying long-term easing; safer: reported at 15.6% in NHMS 2023, lower than 18.3% in 2019.
claims.stale_check: No stale issue; 2025 paper still reports 15.6% (2023) and 18.3% (2019).

claims.claim: Headlines called it the epidemic easing.
claims.source: No primary source found for a headline/official claim that the epidemic was easing.
claims.correction: Remove or rephrase as interpretation, not a media characterisation.

claims.claim: The headline rate counts the diagnosed.
claims.source: NHMS 2023 Fact Sheet: 15.6% = known diabetes 9.7% + raised blood glucose among not-known 5.9%.
claims.correction: Replace with: the rate includes both known diabetes and survey-detected raised blood glucose among people not known to have diabetes.

claims.claim: About 11 million people now carry excess weight.
claims.source: No primary NHMS/MOH source; Sinar Daily (secondary) reported 11 million, 4 June 2024.
claims.correction: Remove the figure or cite as secondary; safer: more than half of adults, 54.4%, are overweight or obese.

claims.claim: Excess weight is the strongest driver of type 2 diabetes.
claims.source: WHO and NIDDK list overweight as a major risk factor among several (inactivity, genetics, age).
claims.correction: Replace 'strongest driver' with 'a major modifiable risk factor'.

claims.claim: Two in five Malaysians with diabetes do not know they have it.
claims.source: NHMS 2023 Key Findings, Decoding diabetes page.
claims.correction: Specify: two in five adults with diabetes detected in NHMS 2023 did not know they had it.

claims.claim: Among those aged 18 to 29, about 84% are unaware.
claims.source: NHMS 2023 Key Findings: 84% of adults aged 18-29 with diabetes do not know they have it.
claims.correction: Specify the denominator: among adults aged 18-29 who have diabetes.

claims.claim: One in two adults lead sedentary lives.
claims.source: NHMS 2023 Fact Sheet sedentary behaviour 49.9%; Key Findings: 1 in 2 adults sedentary.

claims.claim: About 84% take part in no sport, fitness or leisure activity.
claims.source: NHMS 2023 Key Findings: 84% not active in sports, fitness and leisure.

claims.claim: The unverified changed-measurement-definition claim was dropped; no card asserts why the 2019 to 2023 figure fell.
claims.source: Cards assert no cause. NHMS 2019 reanalysed 2011/2015 to a new cut-off, but no card claims a 2019-2023 definition change.
claims.correction: Keep the omission; do not introduce a cause unless the NHMS 2023 technical report supports it.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: Headlines called it the epidemic easing.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: No source shows headlines framed the epidemic as easing.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: The headline rate counts the diagnosed.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: 15.6% = known 9.7% + raised blood glucose among not-known 5.9%; not diagnosed-only.
Not in primary NHMS/MOH material; secondary media only.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: the strongest driver of type 2 diabetes
cardinal_sin_flags.why: 'Strongest driver' overstates the ranking the cited sources support.
Unawareness is high among young diabetics, but prevalence increases with age.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: A health system can lower a diabetes number for a year.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Implies a causal explanation not established by NHMS.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: it sits upstream of every clinic visit.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: 'Every clinic visit' is unsupported and overbroad.

omitted_facts: NHMS 2023 15.6% includes known diabetes 9.7% and raised blood glucose among not-known 5.9%. Source: NHMS 2023 Fact Sheet.
NHMS 2019 used fasting blood glucose 7.0 mmol/L and reanalysed 2011/2015 to the new cut-off. Source: NHMS 2019 Fact Sheet.
84% refers to adults aged 18-29 who have diabetes, not 84% of all 18-29s. Source: NHMS 2023 Key Findings.
The 84% 'not active in sports/fitness/leisure' differs from 'physically inactive' (29.9%). Source: NHMS 2023.
Sedentary behaviour is 49.9%, not exactly 50%; 'one in two' is acceptable rounding. Source: NHMS 2023 Fact Sheet.
source_assessment: Relies primarily on NHMS/MOH/IKU, appropriate for the main statistics, with secondary media (CodeBlue, FMT, The Vibes, Sinar Daily) for context. Adequate for a health-data explainer; light on independent epidemiological interpretation, clinician and patient voice, and policy-implementation evidence.
overall_assessment: Core numerical backbone mostly reliable (2023 and 2019 diabetes, overweight/obesity series, sedentary figure, 84% young-adult unawareness). Publication-significant problems: incorrectly says the headline rate counts only the diagnosed; includes an unverified 11 million estimate; overstates excess weight as the strongest driver; uses causal/rhetorical framing NHMS does not prove. Publishable after tightening diagnosed/undiagnosed language, removing or sourcing 11 million, and softening deterministic claims.
